hook: Childers moved from Fortune 20 operations, Amazon's peak IT infrastructure and GE's global virtualization program, into the CIO seat at a precision aerospace manufacturer. His IoT initiative at Meyer Tool, measuring machine productivity and availability on the factory floor, is the kind of applied industrial AI that rarely makes headlines but represents the actual frontier of operational technology in advanced manufacturing.
name: Vern Childers

quote.text: As a change agent who creates a dynamic, responsive, and business-driven IT organization, he has led several groundbreaking initiatives for the company.

reading.body:
Vern Childers represents a career path from hyperscale and Fortune 20 infrastructure into applied industrial AI, where the work is measuring machine productivity on a factory floor rather than training models in a data center.

His trajectory runs through three distinct infrastructure scales. At GE Corporate he led virtualization across a global enterprise. At Amazon he managed the IT systems that kept a continental retail operation running during its highest-demand periods, earning the North America Q4 IT Peak Leader recognition three consecutive years. At Meyer Tool, an aerospace and gas turbine component manufacturer, he brought that operational discipline to bear on a narrower and more physical problem: knowing, in real time, whether a precision machine is working, idle, or down.

The IoT program at Meyer Tool is the work the data actually describes, and it connects directly to the compute-buildings-power chain, though at its far edge. Factory-floor sensing generates the operational data that feeds machine learning models, but the data here covers only the sensing layer, not what sits above it. What the record does show is a pattern of infrastructure leadership applied progressively closer to physical production, which is where industrial AI must eventually land to matter.
